newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere A shares at record low in Beiru.
newsitem.headline: Solidere A shares at record low in Beiru.

text.p: Solidere A shares fell in the week ended on Friday to an all time low of $10.25 while Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce shares continued their rally.

The A shares, which began trading on the Beirut Secondary Market at $111 in June 1994, had last hit an all-time low of $103 on August 16, 1996 -- or $10.3 after Solidere's 10-for-one stock split which took effect earlier this month.
It was the first time the A shares had hit a record low since the company moved it shares to the Beirut Stock Exchange on September 30.
Solidere B shares were unchanged from last weeks's $11.25.
BLC shares continued a rally begun since listing on the exchange on December 30, rising to $12.375 on Friday compared with $12.25 last week.
Although BLC shares have risen from $11.25 when they began trading, weekly turnover in the bank's shares fell sharply to 21,063 shares against last week's 49,000 shares.
Some 11,034 BLC shares also changed hands on the BSE in block trades during the week for a value of $136,003 compared with 17,500 shares for $211,563 last week.
BLC is the first commercial bank to list on the Beirut exchange since the market reopened a year ago and next Monday Banque Audi will offer 4,158,000 shares for trading on the market.

"I think investors want to see the alternatives for investing on the market and so most are waiting for the listing of new stocks. Banque Audi will trade on Monday and Byblos Bank is expected to list soon," a dealer said.
Weekly turnover in Solidere shares rose to 157,103 shares from last week's 102,180 and value was $1,705,597 from $1,145,910.625.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.76 percent on the week to 80.98 and the BLOM stock index fell 2.57 percent to 909.11.
